html:
The Bunuba are an Aboriginal Australian people of the southern Kimberley in Western Australia, in the limestone ranges around Windjana Gorge, Tunnel Creek and Fitzroy Crossing. The map shows them as Punuba from 1600 to 1815.

Their neighbours included the Gooniyandi, whose language is related to theirs, the Unggumi and Wurla to the north and the Nyikina to the west.

Cattle and sheep stations moved into their country in the 1880s. The Bunuba are best known for the resistance of Jandamarra, a young Bunuba man who had worked as a police tracker. In 1894 he shot a police constable, freed Aboriginal prisoners and led an armed fight against the settlers from the gorges for nearly three years. He was killed at Tunnel Creek in 1897. His story is now told as a Bunuba hero's story, and a play and books have been made about him.
